mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 3-month federal funds rate over the next 60 days indicates a shift toward accommodative monetary policy, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value of expected equity cash flows, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the 3-month federal funds rate above 5.25% in the next 20 days signals tightening policy, raising discount rates and compressing equity present values, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 20-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment (PAYEMS) over the next 5 days indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 5-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly employment (PAYEMS) below 200,000 in the next 5 days signals labor market weakness, reducing consumer and business confidence and lowering earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.

failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 20-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03.
